query: Which material can be used for superconducting properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Yttrium Barium Copper Oxide (YBCO) can exhibit superconducting properties at low temperatures due to its perovskite crystal structure, which facilitates the formation of Cooper pairs and thus superconductivity.
generation.intervention: Cooling YBCO to a temperature below its critical temperature (Tc) of approximately 93 K
generation.conditions: Zero external magnetic field, atmospheric pressure
generation.structural_mediator: Perovskite crystal structure with Cu-O planes
generation.mechanism: Formation of Cooper pairs through electron-phonon interactions, leading to zero electrical resistance
generation.predicted_outcome: A decrease in electrical resistance to zero at temperatures below 93 K, with a transition width of less than 1 K, relative to a baseline of normal conducting materials like copper
generation.uncertainty: The exact critical temperature and transition width may vary depending on the specific composition and crystal structure of the YBCO sample, as well as any potential defects or impurities

falsification_experiment.design: Measure the electrical resistance of a YBCO sample as a function of temperature, using a four-probe method
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the electrical resistance does not drop to zero at temperatures below 92 K, or if the transition width exceeds 2 K, then the hypothesis is falsified
